Abstract:

A typical Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) system integrates sensing nodes, edge gateways, cloud services, analytics, and remote users for continuous industrial monitoring and decision support. The usefulness of this information depends not only on sensing and prediction accuracy, but also on the authenticity of the source, vibrant and innovative communication, clear and crisp messaging, protection against replay attacks, confidentiality and integrity of the transmitted data, reliable delivery, and controlled user access. This investigation develops a progressive gateway-centric framework that addresses these requirements throughout the entire monitoring path. The first contribution establishes a low-cost intelligent air-quality monitoring platform using heterogeneous sensors, a Raspberry Pi gateway, cloud connectivity, machine-learning prediction, and mobile monitoring. The second contribution introduces device-oriented authentication, progressing from FPGA-based PUF authentication to lightweight hybrid fingerprinting and a profile-assisted hash-domain framework for ESP32 nodes. The third contribution develops a complete node-to-gateway mutual-authentication protocol using hardware-UID binding, challenge-conditioned timing verification, persistent freshness, Hash-Based Message Authentication Code (HMAC) based responses, fresh session-key establishment, and Ascon-AEAD128-protected sensor communication. The fourth contribution extends protection from the gateway to the cloud through AES-256-GCM, certificate-validated HTTPS, acknowledgment-controlled store-and-forward delivery, provenance preservation, multi-factor user authentication, Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), alerts, and tamper-evident auditing. Hardware prototypes using ESP32 nodes, Raspberry Pi gateways, and an Oracle Cloud deployment validate the proposed mechanisms. Together, these investigations present an end-to-end research progression, moving from smart, sustainable and Intelligent IIoT monitoring towards secure communication systems comprising authentication, confidentiality, data freshness, resilience, and accountability.

Keywords:&nbsp AES-GCM, Ascon, device authentication, device fingerprinting, gateway computing, Industrial Internet of Things, mutual authentication, secure cloud communication.
